key_insight: A dual-resonator silver microcavity can simultaneously boost sensitizer absorption and direct upconverted emission, overcoming the usual tradeoff in solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion.
engineering_relevance: This architecture could improve low-light photovoltaic and optoelectronic devices by extracting more usable photons from sub-bandgap light without requiring high sensitizer loading.
method: Thermally co-evaporated a rubrene:palladium phthalocyanine (PdPC) active layer inside a planar silver microcavity.
Aligned one dispersive cavity mode with the PdPC absorption peak to enhance sensitizer absorption.
Used a second cavity mode to directionally out-couple upconverted emission while managing reabsorption losses.
evidence_signal: At a cavity angle of 32°, absorptance at 665 nm increased 12-fold, producing a 22-fold peak and 4.5-fold integrated enhancement in detected upconversion emission.
watch_item: Performance may depend on precise cavity-angle/mode alignment, and reabsorption losses can still limit gains if the optical design is not carefully tuned.
paper_title: Dual-Resonator Organic Microcavities for Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
